question: Which of the following are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bryophytes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bryophytes are considered the first group of plants to show a significant step from aquatic to terrestrial life.
 
• They are non-vascular plants, meaning they do not have specialized tissues for water and nutrient transport.
 
• Bryophytes include mosses, liverworts, and hornworts, and they typically inhabit moist environments.
 
• These plants play a crucial role in preventing soil erosion and maintaining soil moisture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gymnosperms**

 
 
• These are seed-producing plants that do not form flowers. Their seeds are not enclosed within a fruit.
 
• Examples include conifers like pine, spruce, and fir.
 
• Gymnosperms have vascular tissues, which help in the transport of water and nutrients.
 
• They are primarily found in temperate and boreal forests.
 
 
 
• **Thallophytes**
 
 
• This group includes algae, fungi, and lichens.
 
• They are non-vascular plants and do not show any differentiation into roots, stems, or leaves.
 
• Thallophytes are primarily aquatic and play a significant role in aquatic ecosystems.
 
• They are important for their role in photosynthesis, nutrient cycling, and as a food source for various organisms.
 
 
 
• **Pteridophytes**
 
 
• These are vascular plants that reproduce via spores and do not produce seeds or flowers.
 
• They include ferns, horsetails, and club mosses.
 
• Pteridophytes have well-differentiated structures like roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They are typically found in moist and shaded environments.
